findings.message: The generated entropy expression calls otherwise() on F.sum(...), rather than on the inner F.when(...). Spark rejects this because otherwise requires a conditional expression, so any pipeline requesting ENTROPY fails during execution. Move otherwise inside sum, or use coalesce for an aggregate-level default. See [Column.otherwise](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/python/reference/pyspark.sql/api/pyspark.sql.Column.otherwise.html).

The generator never applies TimeField.target_granularity. A supported DAILY-to-MONTHLY configuration still groups by individual dates, creates daily MOB rows, and interprets a three-month window as three observed days. Normalize the time column consistently before building MOB, Layer 2A, and Layer 2B.

Building periods only from observed facts compresses calendar gaps. With monthly facts in January, June, and July, July's three-period window includes January, and PREV_MES at June reads January. Generate a complete calendar at the target granularity so row offsets correspond to the configured time units.

MODE returns an arbitrary category instead of the modal category. After grouping by category, first() neither considers frequency nor the aggregated measurement, and its result can change after a shuffle. Select the category associated with the dominant aggregate, with a defined tie-breaker. See [first documentation](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/python/reference/pyspark.sql/api/pyspark.sql.functions.first.html).

DistributionalSpaceBuilder includes FECHA measurements with MAX/MIN aggregators, but this unconditional total attempts to sum the resulting DATE/TIMESTAMP values. Spark cannot sum dates, so a valid dataset containing a date measurement and a distributional categorical fails even when only MODE is requested. Handle temporal measurements explicitly and avoid constructing unused numeric shares.

CREC is allowed by TemporalOutputContract and generated by default for FECHA columns, but this numeric formula compares a date/timestamp with integer zero and divides by a date/timestamp. Spark rejects those operand types, preventing otherwise valid date-measurement pipelines from executing. Emit a temporal-specific expression for temporal sources.

Category values and field names are interpolated into Python literals without escaping. An allowed value containing a double quote produces invalid Python, while backslashes can silently change the comparison value. Generated aliases repeat this problem throughout the script. Serialize every emitted string literal with repr() or an equivalent safe encoder.

Generated column references do not escape Spark identifiers. A valid category value such as A.B produces an alias like SUM__amount__kind_A.B, which F.col interprets as a multipart reference rather than the literal column name. Layer 3 consequently fails to resolve it. Backtick-quote complete identifiers and escape embedded backticks; see [Spark identifier rules](https://spark.apache.org/docs/3.5.6/sql-ref-identifier.html).

An empty feature list emits a standalone comma inside select(), producing invalid Python. This occurs with a supported operators_override that disables all temporal operators. The same rendering bug affects Layer 2A when aggregator overrides produce no pivot columns. Handle empty lists explicitly; simply removing the comma from an empty agg() call would still leave an invalid Spark aggregation.

CREC ignores window_size and direction: every feature compares against lag(..., 1). Consequently time_windows=[3, 6] produces identical three-period and six-period growth features, while FORWARD growth still reads backward. Use the requested horizon and direction when selecting the comparison period.

Non-nullness is not an activity predicate for numeric or FLAG sources. For flag values [1, 0, 0], FREQ returns 3 instead of 1; the same predicate in REC returns 0 instead of 2, because zero-valued periods reset recency. XM repeats this predicate too. Use source-type-appropriate activity conditions so zero flags and zero activity are excluded.

RATIO emits exactly the same expression as SUM_U, with no denominator or division. Every pipeline enabling composed_windows therefore receives window sums labeled as ratios. Implement the ratio calculation, including denominator handling, before exposing this operator.

AbstractDataset explicitly supports a SQL query as source_reference, but every source read is emitted as spark.read.table(...). Passing a supported SELECT query therefore makes Spark parse the query text as a table identifier and fail. Resolve query sources through spark.sql() consistently across all build steps.

Changing generate()'s return annotation to object violates the base method's FeatureStoreOutput return contract. The repository's mypy CI check will reject this override and accesses such as result.code in the new tests. Preserve the FeatureStoreOutput return annotation.
